previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, and type 2 diabetes was admitted due to elevated liver enzymes concerning for transplant rejection. Initial ultrasound showed patent hepatic vasculature, coarsened liver texture, and moderate ascites. A liver biopsy confirmed acute cellular rejection, prompting treatment with IV methylprednisolone, increased tacrolimus, and initiation of mycophenolate mofetil. A second biopsy showed improvement. During admission, she developed steroid-induced hyperglycemia requiring insulin therapy, and a urinary tract infection with Klebsiella pneumoniae and Citrobacter koseri was treated. Her kidney function declined (creatinine up to 1.8), leading to holding of Lasix. She underwent therapeutic paracentesis for symptomatic ascites, which was sterile. She was transitioned to oral prednisone, carvedilol for blood pressure and variceal prophylaxis, and discharged home with close follow-up for tacrolimus monitoring and steroid tapering.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old woman with history of HCV cirrhosis and 
hepatocellular carcinoma s/p transplant complicated by moderate 
acute cellular rejection in the setting of brief tacrolimus 
noncompliance, recurrent hepatitis C now cured and cirrhosis 
complicated by portal hypertension, ascites, and hepatic 
encephalopathy, who presented with diarrhea, decreased appetite, 
and weight loss found to have neutropenia and acute kidney 
injury.

# Diarrhea: Patient presented with ___ BM/daily with weight loss 
and worsening metabolic acidosis despite compliance to oral 
bicarbonate. The patient underwent a broad infectious workup 
including blood cultures, stool cultures and C difficile testing 
which were negative. CMV VL was also sent and was negative. 
However due to continued concern for CMV colitis the patient 
underwent an EGD/colonoscopy which was notable for histologic 
evidence of ischemic colitis. This can be seen as a very rare 
finding from MMF use. The patient was transitioned to myfortic 
180 mg BID with rapid improvement in diarrhea. Metabolic 
acidosis also improved with improvement in diarrhea. 

# ___ on CKD: Patient with creatinine of 2.6 on arrival that 
improved to 2.2 with sodium bicarbonate hydration from recent 
baseline ~1.9-2.2. During her last admission ___, Cr 
uptrended to 1.8 on discharge from baseline 1.3-1.6 thought to 
be secondary to increased tacrolimus dose and Bactrim effect. 
Diuretics were held. The patient continued to improve with 
hydration suggestive of pre renal ___ and not 
consistent with HRS. Bactrim was held, though given stable Cr of 
1.5 Bactrim was restarted prior to discharge. 

# Pancytopenia/Severe Neutropenia: Baseline WBC count of ___ in 
last month. On ___ patient with severe neutropenia and ANC of 
435. This was thought most likely from medication effect. There 
was no evidence of worsening cirrhosis or systemic CMV infection 
with negative VL. The patient's ANC continued to improve with 
down titration of both tacroliums and MMF. However in setting of 
mild transaminitis and transition to myfortic 180 BID, the 
patient had a mild drop in ANC. ANC on discharge was 924. The 
patient was moderate risk for CMV (donor positive, recipient 
positive). Valcyte was subsequently discontinued, and the 
patient will need to have weekly CMV VL drawn (and if CMV+ then 
will need to restart anti-virals). 

# OLT c/b recurrent HCV CIRRHOSIS: HCV cirrhosis and 
hepatocellular carcinoma s/p transplant complicated by moderate 
acute cellular rejection in the setting of brief tacrolimus 
noncompliance, recurrent hepatitis C now cured and cirrhosis 
complicated by portal hypertension, ascites, and hepatic 
encephalopathy. The patient was continued on prednisone 10 mg 
daily. ImmunKnow testing was sent and found to be low. MMF was 
decreased to 250 BID due to concern for contribution to 
neutropenia, and as above patient had marked improvement in 
diarrhea suggestive of MMF colitis. However the patient was 
noted to have mild elevation in LFTS during the admission. MMF 
was transitioned to Myfortic 180 BID. Tacrolimus was also 
titrated to 3 mg BID. The patient maintained a stable mild 
elevation in LFTs. Despite the abnormal LFTS, inpatient biopsy 
was deferred, given no further available interventions as the 
patient is already on prednisone, has leukopenia/neutropenia, 
and is not a candidate for ATG. Valcyte was discontinued. The 
patient will be discharged with close clinic follow up with 
weekly CMV VL, with possible consideration of outpatient biopsy.

# Non-gap acidosis: Patient found to have a bicarbonate 14 on 
admission that improved with intravenous sodium bicarbonate, 
attributed fro ___ on CKD and diarrhea. This remained stable 
throughout the admission, and the patient was continued on PO 
bicarbonate.

# Hepatic encephalopathy: History of hepatic encephalopathy post 
transplant. The patient remained clear without signs of 
encephalopathy. Continued on lactulose PRN and rifaximin.

# GIB/Varices: Last EGD in ___ with 2 cords of grade II 
varices. Previously on nadolol, held during last admission for 
___ cirrhosis. Since transitioned to carvedilol, 
which was continued throughout the admission. The patient 
underwent repeat EGD during the admission which revealed 2 cords 
of grade I varices in the distal esophagus. There was no 
evidence of acute bleeding during the admission. 

# Severe malnutrition: The patient presented with weight loss 
and poor appetite. TSH was within normal limites. Megace was 
started for appetite stimulation with improvement. Aspirin was 
ensured to be continued given pro coagulant nature of megace. 
Patient's home mirtazapine discontinued in setting of concrn for 
somnolence. The patient was continued on Nepro TID with meals. A 
zinc level was sent due to concern for dysgeusia and low at 50. 
Patient was started on 14 day course of zinc repletion. 

================== 
CHRONIC ISSUES
================== 
# Type II Diabetes: Patient found to be hypoglycemic in clinic. 
Lantus dosing was decreased given concern for hypoglycemia. 
However patient had continued issues with hyperglycemia and home 
insulin regimen was uptitrated including long acting and sliding 
scale. 

# Hypertension: Patient had elevations in BP though secondary to 
initiation of megace. Home carvedilol was increased to 25 mg BID 
with improvement. 

# Osteopenia/Bone Health: Patient continued vitamin D and 
calcium carbonate. 

# Glaucoma: Patient continued latonoprost and timolol. 

# History of Seizure: Patient continued keppra.

Dear Ms. ___,

It was a pleasure caring for you during your stay at ___. You 
were admitted to the hospital with diarrhea, weight loss and 
decreased appetite. Infectious workup was negative. Your kidneys 
showed signs of damage on admission that was likely from 
dehydration from diarrhea and improved with IV fluids.

diarrhea. There was no signs that an infection was the cause of

effect of your medication cell cept. You were switched to a 
different formulation of this medication is called myfortic. 
Your diarrhea was much improved on discharge.

changed the dosing of your immunosuppression, however your blood 
counts remained low. It is very important that if you have any 
signs of fever or cough that you seek immediate medical 
attention by calling your doctor or go to the emergency 
department.

with your appetite. This caused an elevation in your blood 
sugars and your insulin was increased.

We wish you the best!
